title: A new year of service
summary: Began the 2026–2027 term as Sergeant-at-Arms for the First Bahamas Branch of Toastmasters Club 1600.
impact: Term responsibilities include meeting readiness, protocol, hospitality, member experience and support for the club's executive agenda. Ongoing delivery is tracked separately.
highlights: Induction and introduction as Sergeant-at-Arms
Committed to serving both club members and the wider community
Supported meeting protocol, guest welcome and the operations agenda
credit: Service under President Toastmaster Azano Major, alongside the 2026–2027 Executive Team.

title: 15th Annual Neil Percentie Back2School Jamboree
summary: Helped prepare and deliver Club 1600's annual back-to-school community initiative at Union Village Park.
impact: The club distributed 200 student packages, prepared 50 teacher packages, provided 1,500+ additional loose school items and engaged an estimated 150+ attendees. School-supply, grooming, dental and family activities supported the wider community.
highlights: Worked on the package preparation crew with Charles Rose and Jonathan Smith
Assisted setup alongside Tyler Collie, Eddie Toote, Jonathan Smith and Dominic Strachan
Participated in breakdown/cleanup with fellow members
Coordinated in-kind logistical contributions including chairs, tables, tent and coolers
Supported a club-wide event sustained over 15 annual editions
credit: A collective Club 1600 effort with members, Quintin Percentie, Percy's Island Game ($5,000 donation), community partners and volunteers.

title: The work before the gavel
summary: Meeting-room preparation, welcoming guests and conducting Sergeant-at-Arms ceremonial duties across weekly meetings.
impact: Meeting-opening responsibilities are documented in multiple August and September club minutes. An end-of-year count of meetings and guests is still to be added.
highlights: Meeting readiness and front-of-room protocol
Calling regular meetings to order
Coordination with the Social & Reception Committee
Attention to guest experience and room standards
credit: The club's weekly meeting experience is delivered with fellow officers, committee members and volunteers.

title: Tracking the cost of service
summary: Consolidated SAA receipts, categorized spending and developed an approach for tracking reimbursables and receivables.
impact: The ongoing register supports cleaner reconciliation and future handovers. Final period totals should be verified from the finance tracker before publication.
highlights: Categorized submitted receipts
Separated amounts paid from amounts receivable
Started a repeatable finance-tracking structure
credit: Financial figures are managed with the club's wider accountability and reporting process.

title: The SAA initiatives roadmap
summary: Mapped a multi-quarter pipeline spanning member experience, social events, club presentation standards and infrastructure.
impact: A working roadmap for Q1–Q4; future concepts are not counted as completed initiatives until delivered.
highlights: Social and fellowship programming
Guest chair-cover and step-and-repeat presentation improvements
Member-facing website and engagement tools
Future community and networking concepts
credit: Ideas are subject to executive approval, feasibility and available support.

title: Setting the standard
summary: Produced member-facing visual guidance on Club 1600's expected meeting attire.
impact: A simple reference for suits, ties, Toastmasters pins and preferred dress shoes, reinforcing the club's professional presentation standards.
highlights: Designed and refined the dress-code graphic
Prepared a concise WhatsApp reminder for members
Clarified the preferred meeting look
credit: Created to support established Club 1600 meeting standards.

title: Evaluation Contest Masterclass
summary: Developed and refined a structured evaluation-contest training presentation for Cable Revolutionaries Toastmasters Club.
impact: Completed a reorganized teaching deck and aligned speaker notes; delivery results and attendance can be added if confirmed.
highlights: Organized evaluation methods into a natural learning sequence
Developed a white-background presentation with more dynamic visual hierarchy
Prepared speaker notes corresponding to the training slides
credit: Speaking and education work beyond Club 1600, included as part of the Toastmasters year.

title: Club 1600's digital home
summary: Worked on a modern web presence for Club 1600, including leadership, resources, gallery and community-impact content.
impact: Web pages and assets have been developed in the club1600.org GitHub repository. Public deployment and remaining media tasks should be checked before final impact claims.
highlights: Homepage and leadership features
Photo gallery and resource sections
Community Impact content for the Neil Percentie initiative
Modern styling and mobile-conscious navigation
credit: The wider club and executive team provided the people, mission and content represented.

title: A meeting beyond our usual walls
summary: Prepared member-facing logistics and signage for a Club 1600 meeting hosted at the Office of the Prime Minister.
impact: Provided guest parking guidance, entrance support directions, third-floor room instructions and a notice for the usual Red Cross meeting location.
highlights: Coordinated messaging about the temporary meeting-location change
Clarified front and back guest entry routes
Prepared professional attire guidance and visitor directions
Produced a venue-change notice
credit: Supported the executive and the Social & Reception Committee's meeting logistics.

title: 1600 Degreez — Q1 Social & Family Fun Day
summary: Developed the event concept, invitations and detailed run of show for the Q1 member-and-family gathering at Bernard Hanna, DTM's beach property.
impact: Event date was October 3. Final attendance, photo record and event outcomes are awaiting a post-event recap; these are not yet included as verified results.
highlights: Designed and refined a coordinated flyer campaign
Planned grilled food, family games and music
Prepared Table Topics, raffle, football lounge, dominoes and backgammon programming
Coordinated a planned massage station and event supplies checklist
Rescheduled and communicated the updated date
credit: Planned with club members, volunteers and support from Bernard Hanna, DTM. Event outcomes to be confirmed.

title: Making the next social bigger
summary: Began early outreach for beverage contributions, pricing and possible entertainment elements for the Q2 social.
impact: Planning-stage work only. Proposed additions, including a fire dancer, are under exploration rather than confirmed bookings.
highlights: Initial conversations about drink donations
Exploring discounts and vendor prices
Researching additional entertainment options, including a fire dancer
credit: Potential features are subject to venue, budget and executive decisions.

title: District 47 — Florida bound
summary: Developed a visual campaign to build interest in a potential Club 1600 delegation to the District 47 conference in spring 2027.
impact: April 2027 is a working target period, not a confirmed conference date. Final travel, venue and attendee details will be documented later.
highlights: Created initial conference-trip flyer concepts
Explored a Florida-bound visual identity and member photo treatment
Encouraged planning for a stronger club delegation
credit: An early Club 1600 interest-building effort; official District 47 conference details pending.

title: On a Sunday, We Golf!
summary: Introduced a recurring Sunday opportunity for members to learn golf, practice their swing and connect outside regular meetings.
impact: Weekly meetup announced for Sundays, 3–5 PM, at the Blue Hills/Baillou Hills Sports Complex Golf Range. Attendance figures are not yet logged.
highlights: Developed and refined a member-facing golf social flyer
Set the weekly Sunday 3–5 PM meetup
Wrote the introductory group invitation
Made beginner participation central to the message
credit: Open invitation for Club 1600 members to participate and strengthen fellowship.

title: Trudy's Thru Out Da Week
summary: Introduced a laid-back weekly member hangout, prioritizing Monday evenings at Trudy's Bar & Grill.
impact: Members were invited to connect every Monday from 8 PM, with flexibility to meet at other times. Attendance and frequency will be updated as sessions take place.
highlights: Developed a separate social flyer with venue photography
Established Mondays at 8 PM as the primary weekly meet-up
Promoted informal fellowship without a formal meeting agenda
credit: A casual member-led opportunity to build relationships beyond Thursday meetings.
